## Your task: P9 E7 — notifications, outbound webhooks and function triggers (`SRV-062`, `SRV-063`, `FN-025`)

**Resume, do not restart.** A previous agent's unfinished, unreviewed work is saved as `docs/plans/p9-handoff/E7-notify.patch.gz` (made against `fcafe9a`). After rule 0 apply it without its generated files:
`gunzip -c docs/plans/p9-handoff/E7-notify.patch.gz | git apply --3way --exclude='*.pb.go' --exclude='*.connect.go' --exclude='*/dbgen/*' --exclude='docs/reference/*'`
then resolve conflicts by hand: `backend/internal/auth/rbac.go` and `rbac_p9.go` already hold every P9 permission (use `NotificationsManage`, `WebhooksManage`; drop any const block the patch adds); its migration `0024_notifications.sql` becomes the next free number (0026…); then `make gen`. Review the applied code critically before building on it — fix anything below the code standard. It stopped while writing `backend/internal/function/triggers.go` (the notify import just added).

Read: `docs/plans/p9.md` lines 521–535 (§5.7); `docs/adr/0081-*.md`; `docs/engineering/security-practices.md` (grep the SSRF section); `backend/internal/httpx` (heads); `backend/internal/function` (greps for how server invocation authenticates — a workload identity; never widen privileges); `schema/limits.json` keys `webhooks.perOrg`, `notifications.perHour`.

Deliver:
1. **`backend/internal/notify`:** a typed event registry other milestones publish to (`notify.Publish(ctx, Event)`): approval requested, release published, rollout paused, lock requested, function failing, alert fired, break-glass used, licence expiring; per-user and per-team subscriptions; channels: in-app inbox (stored, read/unread, API + CLI), SMTP (`net/smtp`, STARTTLS required unless explicitly disabled for development, with a distinct warning), Slack, Microsoft Teams and Telegram through the SSRF-safe client; `notifications.perHour` limit; delivery log; `PLX-8400` misconfigured channel. Channel credentials live in the secret store, never in logs or API responses.
2. **Outbound webhooks (Standard Webhooks):** headers `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature` (`v1,` + base64 HMAC-SHA256 over `id.timestamp.body`); secrets `whsec_`-prefixed, rotatable with an overlap window (both signatures sent); `webhooks.perOrg` limit; durable PostgreSQL queue drained by the worker with exponential backoff and full jitter for up to 24 h, delivery log, `PLX-8401` after giving up; verified against the published Standard Webhooks test vectors embedded as testdata.
3. **Function triggers (`FN-025`):** cron schedules on function aliases (in-house parser: 5 fields plus `@hourly/@daily/@weekly/@monthly`, UTC or IANA zone, DST-correct: a skipped local time fires once at the next valid instant, a repeated one fires once), run by the worker with leader election through PostgreSQL advisory locks, idempotent per fire time; inbound webhooks at `/hooks/{app}/{function}` verified by Standard Webhooks signature or a pluggable `Verifier` interface (payment providers use it in P13), replay protection by webhook-id cache plus timestamp tolerance (`PLX-7150` bad cron, `PLX-7151` bad signature, `PLX-7152` replay); body size bounded by the existing request guards; invocation through the existing function service with its workload identity.
4. `proto/plux/v1/notification.proto` + `make gen`; handlers; server wiring (worker role runs the queues and scheduler with clean shutdown); CLI `plux notifications …`, `plux webhooks …`, `plux fn triggers …` following an existing command file's pattern (e.g. `backend/cmd/plux/cmd_governance.go`).

Tests (names carry `SRV_062`/`SRV_063`/`FN_025`): Standard Webhooks vectors, rotation overlap, retry schedule bounds and give-up, SSRF refusal of private destinations, SMTP refusing plaintext, per-hour limit, cron parsing table tests incl. DST gaps and overlaps and invalid expressions, leader election with two schedulers firing once, inbound webhook good/bad signature/replay/stale timestamp, CLI against a test server. Integration tests against PostgreSQL.
